meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Federal incorporation coordination with cantonal registered office; target canton: Zug for enterprise SaaS/Crypto Valley substance)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Civil Code, Swiss Code of Obligations, cantonal administrative law; partially harmonized with EU standards via Bilateral Agreements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 12 November 1986, in force 16 March 1987)
Switzerland–China DTA on Income and Capital (signed 27 January 1990, in force 19 November 1990; Amending Protocol signed 25 September 2013, in force 14 November 2014)
EFTA Convention (Vaduz, 21 June 2001) and EFTA–China FTA (signed 21 December 2013, in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland–EU Free Trade Agreement (1972) and Bilateral Agreements I and II (1999–2004) covering services, trade facilitation and mutual recognition
US–Swiss DTA (signed 2 October 1996, in force 19 December 1997)
Overall Swiss treaty network: 128+ active BITs and over 105 DTAAs per SECO registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA, SR 955.0), as revised effective 1 January 2024 introducing the mandatory Transparency Register for UBO disclosure; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis (money laundering) and Art. 305ter (insufficient financial diligence); Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance of 2 February 2023 (AMLO, SR 955.01); Transparency Register Ordinance of 16 December 2022 (SR 955.013); Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Implementation of International Sanctions of 22 March 2002 (Embargo Act, SR 946.231); Financial Market Supervision Act (FINMASA, SR 956.1). Companies must file UBO declarations within 30 days of formation; subsequent material changes within 30 days.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Statutes) and Incorporation Minutes of the AG
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal notary public in the canton of registered office (e.g., Notariat Zug); foreign notary acceptable only for pre-incorporation signatures under Hague Convention
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (final incorporation notarization performed in Switzerland; foreign signatures apostilled in country of origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Extract from foreign commercial register of each corporate founder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in country of origin (e.g., Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry, US Secretary of State, Chinese SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified translation into German, French, Italian or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all founding shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuance authority plus notary public of the holder's residence jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of blocked capital deposit (Sperrkonto) covering minimum paid-in share capital and, if applicable, attached Swiss bank KYC beneficial owner forms
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss FINMA-licensed bank or securities firm holding the subscription funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Swiss-issued notarized bank confirmation; no apostille required internally

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, signatories and UBOs against: (i) State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions list; (ii) FINMA sanctions and enforcement register; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List as implemented under the Swiss Embargo Act; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List for EU nexus; (v) OFAC SDN for USD payment rails via Stripe/Wise; (vi) UK HMT sanctions for GBP exposure. PEP treatment: foreign and domestic PEPs require enhanced due diligence under AMLA Art. 4 and AMLO Art. 12, including documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification; family members and close associates assimilated to the PEP. The low-risk B2B SaaS model does not remove the duty to file STR reports with the Swiss Financial Intelligence Unit (MROS) when suspicion exists.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – Zentraler Firmenindex (official federal central business index, www.zefix.ch) operated by the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI); preliminary name clearance is processed through the competent cantonal commercial register office, e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950–952 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), the AG must include the mandatory legal form designation 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (or French/Italian equivalents 'SA'; phonetic variants tolerated only in Latin script); the name must be true, clear, self-explanatory and non-misleading; naming may use Latin script in German, French, Italian or English/third languages, provided transliteration into Latin script is used and the firm name describes the B2B SaaS business with sufficient specificity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca – requires FINMA banking license prior to approval
Insurance / Assurance / Versicherung – requires FINMA insurance license
Fund / Fonds / Anlagefonds – requires CISA/FINMA asset management authorization
Trust / Fiduciaire / Treuhand – requires licensing under Financial Institutions Act (FinIA) for fiduciary services; otherwise misleading
Swiss / Suisse / Svizzera / Schweizer – requires IPI federal authorization and may trigger federal watch protection
Federal / Bund / Eidgenossenschaft / Confédération – implies state authority and is rejected
Canton / Kanton / Municipal / Gemeinde – implies cantonal or municipal authority and is rejected
Public / Öffentlich / State / Staats – implies public-law nature and is misleading
Pension / Vorsorge / Retirement / Altersvorsorge – implies regulated pension management
Holding / Participations – permitted only if the company genuinely operates a holding function, otherwise rejected as misleading
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registrar issues a formal decision with grounds. Within 30 days of service, the applicant may (i) submit a written reconsideration request with the cantonal commercial register office, proposing minor amendments; (ii) file an administrative appeal to the Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht des Kantons Zug); (iii) after exhaustion of cantonal remedies, file a public-law appeal to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) in Lausanne if constitutional or federal-law rights are violated. A single 90-day extension of the reservation is available on request and payment of the statutory extension fee before expiry; if the window lapses, the name is released and a new request must be filed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop_note: Estimated appeal legal fees: CHF 500–3,000 depending on complexity; recommended alternative is to refile an amended name to avoid incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial acceptance: a professional domiciliation address (Sitzdomizil) provided by a licensed Swiss corporate services firm in the canton of registration is recognized by the commercial register and permitted for a B2B SaaS AG, provided the domiciliary maintains physical records, accepts official service, and the AG administratively operates in Switzerland. A purely virtual foreign mailbox or non-Swiss business address is legally void; it leads to cancellation of the registered seat, loss of Swiss tax residence, fines, and potential director criminal liability under Art. 152–154 of the Swiss Criminal Code and Art. 955 OR. The AG must in practice maintain at least a verifiable Swiss administrative presence, including a board of directors with Swiss meeting activity where required, to satisfy the head-office test of Art. 618 OR.

Publication in Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / SHAB) of the incorporation notice
Transparency Register (UBO) initial filing and due diligence documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, consular legalization, and certified translation of foreign corporate founder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Appropriate authority in country of origin plus Swiss certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (approx. CHF 280 per founder document package; apostille CHF 30–80 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service, first year (physical address, mail handling, registered agent, UBO compliance support)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss corporate services provider in Zug
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Swiss AG with commercial substance (approx. CHF 7,500/year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate counsel due diligence, PEP/sanctions screening, name strategy, and incorporation legal drafting (fixed fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for standard Swiss AG in IT services (approx. CHF 5,000)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 610-763 (stock corporation), formation: Arts. 626-635, Commercial Register entry: Arts. 927-936; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); Art. 950-956 OR on corporate name; Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax and cantonal tax notification provisions
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce), acting under the supervisory authority of the Federal Office for Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz); official publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/FOSC)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation drawn up before a cantonal notary (öffentliche Urkunde / acte authentique) and electronic application for entry in the Commercial Register (Gründungsmeldung / requête d'inscription au registre du commerce)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An AG requires minimum total share capital of CHF 100,000 under Art. 621 OR. At incorporation, shares must be paid in cash to at least 20% of nominal value and in all events at least CHF 50,000 must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) held by a Swiss bank or PostFinance; disposal of the escrow is authorized only after Commercial Register entry, and the remaining balance must be fully paid within three months of release under Art. 632 (1)-(2) OR.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding board hereby (1) confirms that all CHF 100,000 share capital is validly subscribed, with CHF 50,000 deposited in escrow per Art. 632(2) OR; (2) adopts the registered office at c/o [Agent], [Street], 6300 Zug, Switzerland; (3) appoints [Name] as Board President, [Name] as CEO, and [Name] as Secretary; (4) grants individual and collective signature rights per Art. 718 OR; (5) authorizes the CEO to open bank accounts, apply for VAT and social insurance registration, and execute all actions necessary for Commercial Register entry. The board orders payment of the remaining CHF 50,000 upon release of the escrow.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search, reservation and availability clearance with the cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the Swiss ZEFIX central name database operated by the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online ZEFIX search for the proposed company name in the 'Aktiengesellschaft' / 'AG' category to verify uniqueness and non-misleading character under Art. 950 OR. For interim security, submit a written name availability request to the target canton's Handelsregisteramt; the approved name is then fixed in the draft public deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: ZEFIX name search protocol
Written name pre-approval request to the Handelsregisteramt
Passport or ID copy of each founder
Signed power of attorney for the local formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a negative name opinion (Beanstandung), amend the requested name by adding an individualizing element (e.g., a product or group identifier) and resubmit within the stated deadline; any third-party objection is resolved through an administrative decision under Art. 30 HRegV.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public deed of incorporation before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public notary (Amtsnotar / Urkundsperson) competent under cantonal law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the constitutive founders' meeting before the notary in person or by authenticated representation. The notary verifies the identity of all founders, the statutes, the capital coverage, the nature of contributions, and the appointment of the first board of directors and statutory auditor (when applicable). The notary then reads the formation deed and certifies the signatures per Art. 629(2) OR.
required_dossiers: Authenticated passports or identity documents of all founders
Draft articles of association satisfying Arts. 626-628 OR
Blocked escrow bank confirmation issued to the notary (Art. 633 OR)
Auditor acceptance declaration for statutory audit (where required)
Declaration on bearer shares and beneficial ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal deficiencies (e.g., missing beneficial ownership declaration, incomplete founder identification, defective articles), execute a supplementary notarial addendum and re-submit to the same notary for consolidated attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital deposit account and remittance of the minimum paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or PostFinance AG operating under FINMA regulatory supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the pre-formation deposit account in the company's name. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 representing the amount paid up on the subscribed shares. The bank issues a blocked account certificate confirming that funds may be disposed of only upon written authorization of the company after Commercial Register registration, in accordance with Art. 633 OR.
required_dossiers: Notarized draft deed of incorporation
Bank account opening forms including the AMLA/KYC package
Beneficial ownership declaration
Lease agreement or registered office support for the bank file
Passport copies of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further anti-money-laundering documentation, supply the source-of-funds affidavit and corporate structure chart; if account opening is unreasonably delayed, engage a FINMA-licensed fintech escrow agent or escalate through the bank's internal compliance committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutive meeting of the board of directors and appointment of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Aktiengesellschaft under Arts. 716a, 718 and 718a OR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first organizational board meeting after notarization and escrow deposit. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution confirming subscription, registered office, Board President, CEO, Secretary, signing rights, and the release of contribution obligations. Each appointed officer signs the declaration of acceptance for filing with the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution in written form
Officer acceptance declarations
Signing rights matrix and specimen signatures
Auditor acceptance declaration (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointed officer declines the mandate, convene a supplementary board meeting, elect a replacement, and file the corrected appointment declaration; any missing signature specimen is cured by immediate notarized signature verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the Commercial Register application and SHAB publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) through the e-register platform and the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated registration application, annexes, and notarial attestation through the official e-register channel. The registrar verifies compliance with Arts. 629, 632, 634 OR and HRegV. Upon approval, the AG is entered and the publication in SHAB triggers legal personality, release of the blocked escrow account, and the start of company operations.
required_dossiers: Authenticated registration application form with notarial signature
Original public deed of incorporation
Board and auditor acceptance declarations
Bank blocked account certificate
Consent of the registered office owner or lease agreement
ZEFIX name approval evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency query, file a written cure within the statutory cure period supplying the missing annexes; if the objection persists, request a formal decision and appeal to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and cantonal tax, VAT, and social insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), competent cantonal tax office, AHV compensation office, and cantonal social insurance register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon legal personality, the AG receives automatic notification duties. File the VAT registration with ESTV when annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (Art. 10 VAT Act) or apply voluntarily earlier; coordinate cantonal corporate income tax registration; register the company's UID and, if staff are hired, employee AHV/Social insurance registration with the regional compensation fund within statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug)
Final notarized deed and articles of association
ESTV VAT registration form with turnover projection
Cantonal tax registration form
UID business identification number request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ESTV or the cantonal tax administration queries the turnover estimate, submit a revised business plan and auditable revenue forecast; any late registration penalty is mitigated by showing compliance intent and filing an immediate cure application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal office notification, occupational safety, and general licensing verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal commercial and building services (Gewerbepolizei), cantonal fire inspection service, EKAS coordination office, and SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an ISIC 6201 enterprise SaaS operation, no industrial license is required under Swiss law. Complete the municipal notification for office use, obtain the fire safety inspection certificate for the leased premises, contract SUVA accident insurance within 30 days of the first employee's hiring, and prepare the workplace risk assessment under EKAS guideline 6508.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and floor plan for office premises
Cantonal fire inspection completion certificate
SUVA insurance contract or certificate
EKAS workplace risk assessment
Municipal business notification form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies deviations, implement the corrective measures ordered within 30 days and schedule a re-inspection; no appeal is required as this step is a notification regime rather than a licensing procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 enterprise SaaS development; the relevant office-level contacts are the municipal Gewerbepolizei for notification and the cantonal building/fire inspection departments for premises approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required - no mandatory industrial operating or manufacturing permit under Swiss law for pure enterprise cloud software services; only municipal office-use notification and, where applicable, voluntary certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2) apply

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) acting through the competent cantonal environmental protection agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category: non-listed office/service activity per the EIA Ordinance (UVPV/OPIA); no EIA registration, scoping, or formal report is mandated for a software development office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater discharged to municipal sewer in compliance with cantonal drainage regulations; no stack emission limits or VOC plant thresholds apply because no industrial production occurs; electronic waste and WEEE handled per the Swiss Ordinance on the Return, Taking Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (SR 814.620); CO2 Act monitoring relevant only if an in-house data center is operated

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification completed by the cantonal fire inspection service covering evacuation routes, emergency exits, and fire extinguishing equipment for the office floor; structural load compliance covered by the municipal building permit for the leased space; occupational clearance confirmed through a workplace safety review under EKAS/SUVA guidelines, including electrical safety of IT server equipment, first-aid readiness, and mandatory work-accident insurance registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC). Official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT eServices via ePortal (www.eportal.estv.admin.ch); public UID register via www.uid.admin.ch and company register via www.zefix.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss AG: (1) notarial incorporation and entry in the Cantonal Commercial Register automatically generate the Swiss Business Identifier (UID, format CHE-123.456.789) under the UID Act; (2) VAT registration is filed electronically through the ESTV ePortal using the UID; after approval the UID is extended with the code 'MWST' (TVA/IVA) and constitutes the Swiss VAT number, effective retroactively from the commencement of taxable activity. For a foreign enterprise without a Swiss seat or permanent establishment: (a) appoint a Swiss tax representative (art. 67 VAT Act) who is jointly and severally liable; (b) file the simplified VAT registration application via the ESTV ePortal; (c) obtain a foreign-entity VAT registration number for Swiss-source supplies. No income-tax registration is required for a non-resident shareholder of the CH AG unless a Swiss permanent establishment or Swiss real estate is held; the AG itself must be registered for corporate income tax with the cantonal tax administration of its seat after commercial-register entry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Swiss corporation income tax on worldwide profit, with relief for qualifying participations and foreign permanent-establishment income (territorial exemption). Federal direct tax is 8.5% of post-tax profit (i.e. 7.83% pre-tax); cantonal and communal taxes vary and aggregate effective rates typically range from 11.9% (Zug) to 21.0% (Geneva). No pass-through treatment or federal check-the-box election exists for a Swiss AG; the AG is always taxed at entity level and distributions are additionally subject to Swiss withholding tax (35%). No corporate tax-exempt zones apply to SaaS operations in Switzerland; customs free ports exist only for tangible goods warehousing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no US-style check-the-box election. Available elections and regimes for a CH AG: (1) VAT group taxation (art. 21 VAT Act) for closely linked Swiss entities, treated as a single taxable person; (2) partial taxation procedure (Teilbesteuerungsverfahren) for dividend income, with 50% federal reduction and cantonal reductions ranging from 30% to 60%; (3) participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) for dividend and capital-gain income from qualifying participations of at least 10%; (4) cantonal STAF incentives: patent-box regime ring-fencing qualified patent and similar IP income at a 90% reduction, R&D super-deduction up to 150%, and notional interest deduction on excess equity where the canton has enacted these measures; (5) hybrid mismatch rules are implemented through the Multilateral Instrument preference provisions and treaty-override mechanisms rather than a domestic hybrid-election statute.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuergesetz, MWSTG; SR 641.20). No GST or sales-and-use tax applies at federal level in Switzerland.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 net annual worldwide turnover from taxable activities for enterprises established in Switzerland (art. 10(1) VAT Act). Foreign-established enterprises have no turnover threshold and are taxable from the first franc of Swiss-source turnover unless a simplified registration procedure applies (art. 67 VAT Act). Voluntary registration for Swiss-established SMEs is available from CHF 100,000; sector-specific relief applies to agriculture, non-profit entities and small businesses with turnover below CHF 100,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction-control regime analogous to the Italian Sistema di Interscambio (SdI). Electronic invoicing in B2B flows is voluntarily exchanged under the Swiss SWE-B / eBill XML standard; the QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is the mandatory presentation standard for Swiss payment slips and is widely embedded in SaaS billing platforms; suppliers to the Federal Administration are required to submit e-invoices in the SWE-B standard. For audit purposes the ESTV accepts structured electronic evidence of export transactions, provided the data is complete, authentic and retained for the statutory 10-year record-keeping period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating with full input-VAT deduction applies under art. 23 VAT Act to: (1) physical goods exported by the supplier from Switzerland with customs proof; (2) services, including B2B Enterprise SaaS, whose place of supply is deemed to be outside Switzerland because the recipient is established abroad (art. 18(2)(a) VAT Act, B2B rule); the supplier must demonstrate the recipient's foreign establishment through documentary evidence such as the recipient's foreign VAT/TIN number, official company-register extract, executed contract, invoicing data, payment routing via SWIFT/BIC/IBAN, and IP-geolocation of cloud access; (3) ancillary services directly connected to exported goods. SaaS supplied to a Swiss-established customer is subject to Swiss VAT at 8.1% (8.6% from 1 January 2026) at the recipient's place of establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) filed in the Swiss customs e-dec system for physical goods; not applicable to purely digital SaaS deliveries, as no physical movement of goods occurs
Commercial invoice stating the supplier, foreign recipient, service description, payment currency, and the zero-rating legal basis under art. 23 VAT Act
Proof of foreign establishment of the recipient: foreign VAT/TIN number, company-register extract, or a signed recipient declaration under art. 23(3) VAT Act
Contractual agreement evidencing the B2B SaaS subscription, license scope and cross-border delivery terms
Bank payment trail (SWIFT/IBAN statement or inward remittance credit) evidencing cross-border receipt of consideration
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note when tangible storage media or on-premise appliances are exported as part of the software transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Switzerland imposes no statutory FX-repatriation deadline and maintains no exchange-control regime; the Swiss National Bank only requires statistical reporting of foreign receivables, and export zero-rating is not conditioned on foreign-currency inflow. If the ESTV determines that zero-rating was claimed without valid recipient-establishment proof, the tax deficiency is assessed retroactively for up to 5 years (10 years in cases of intentional evasion), with statutory default interest and full clawback of the unpaid VAT. Intentional tax evasion attracts a fine of up to three times the evaded tax (art. 97(3) VAT Act); gross negligence attracts a fine of up to once the evaded tax (art. 97(2) VAT Act). Where the taxpayer secures an undue tax advantage through forged documents, false statements or deceit, the criminal offence of Abgabebetrug (art. 96 VAT Act) applies and is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years or a monetary penalty of up to CHF 300,000, in addition to the full retrospective clawback and interest. The ESTV's internal audit unit conducts risk-based documentary audits of SaaS exporters, applying heightened scrutiny to recurring cross-border invoices lacking contemporaneous recipient-establishment evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements (SWIFT MT103, Commercial LC)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting resolution approving financial statements and deciding on profit appropriation, recorded in statutory minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and Shareholders' Meeting (Annual General Meeting); no filing to government unless published
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of balance sheet date; Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 699 para 3; typical year-end 31 December => by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board liability; criminal sanction for failure to prepare accounts (Art. 325-ter SCC) up to CHF 10,000; non-approval delays tax filing and exposes company to compulsory dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Publication of audited financial statements and audit report (for companies subject to ordinary audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt) via the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than twelve months after the balance sheet date; Or Art. 699 para 3 CO (12 months after balance sheet date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish is an administrative/register offence; notice from Commercial Registrar with deadline; persistent non-compliance triggers ex officio strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification of beneficial ownership data in the Transparency Register (annual UBO confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Central Transparency Register operated by Federal Office of Justice / Fedpol (electronic register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year with confirmation due 31 December; changes must be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to CHF 100,000 (Art. 60 FINMA no... actually Art. 59?); violation of AML obligations, continuous violation of reporting duties can trigger criminal prosecution and company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return (Federal, Cantonal and Communal taxes, single return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (e.g., Zug/Canton tax office) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after fiscal year end with cantonal extension practice; standard filing autumn (e.g., 31 March-30 June); use current yield: typically 31 March of following year, automatic 2-3 month extensions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default surcharge up to 25% of assessed tax plus interest 3.5%-4.5%; failure to file triggers estimated assessment; persistent delinquency can lead to enforcement measures against the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (annually filed when quarterly not elected) - sales of B2B SaaS exempt? Wait, SaaS is taxable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual VAT filers, return and payment due no later than 31 March for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, penalty up to 3x of the amount? In Swiss VAT, penal surcharge; administrative fines

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss corporate income tax is a three-tier system. Federal direct tax: 8.5% of taxable profit after federal tax (effective 7.83% of pre-tax profit). Cantonal and communal taxes are levied on the same base with pre-tax equivalents varying by domicile: approximately 11.9% combined in Canton Zug, approximately 18.2% in Zurich and approximately 19.7% in Geneva. A Zug-domiciled B2B SaaS AG should budget a combined headline effective rate of roughly 11.9% to 14.5% before incentive deductions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist. Recurring preferential deductions include: (1) cantonal patent/IP box exemption of up to 90% of net qualifying IP income under an OECD nexus formula (Zug combined box rate circa 1.2% to 2.4%); (2) research and development super-deduction of up to 150% of qualifying Swiss R&D costs (Zug and Zurich apply an additional 20% to 50%); (3) notional interest deduction (NID) on excess equity in several cantons including Zug and Zurich; (4) statutory participation exemption removing from the taxable base qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from participations of at least 10% or with acquisition value of at least CHF 1 million; (5) no federal IP box, and no reduced rate for holding companies beyond the participation exemption.
